chunks: From Safwan al-Jammal, he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
The death of a believer leaves a gap in religion.

key_terms.ثَلَّمَ: To make a hole in, to gap, to leave a void
key_terms.رَجُلَ: Man or believer (in this context referring to a specific believer)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of a believer's death in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of a 'notch' or 'crack' (thalam) to describe how the loss of a believer weakens the structural integrity of the faith community, a concept deeply rooted in Shia hadith literature regarding the spiritual weight of the righteous. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Mumin*, underscores the communal responsibility to preserve and honor believers, as their absence leaves a discernible gap in the collective religious fabric. The imagery reflects the Shia understanding of the believer as a pillar of Islam, whose presence stabilizes the community's spiritual and social cohesion.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 75. It has been related that Safwan al-Jammal said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) saying:
The death of a believer leaves a gap in religion.
